summary: Jan Safarewicz was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Vilnius University (PhD circa 1922–1927) and the University of Paris (circa 1927–1931) under Benveniste and Meillet. He held posts at Vilnius University and Jagiellonian University.

Linguist and Indologist Jan Szczepan Otrębski studied at Warsaw, Leipzig, and Jagiellonian University (PhD under Jan Michał Rozwadowski). He held academic posts at Jagiellonian University, Vilnius University, and Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (1947–1960).

Jan T. Ergardt worked in Buddhist and religious studies, completing a PhD at Lund University by 1970 under Rune Edvin Arvid Johansson. He was later affiliated with Lund University as a colleague (attested 1989).

Jan Westerhoff works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from Cambridge (BA, PhD under Michael Potter) and SOAS (PhD), and held posts at Oxford, Durham, and SOAS, among others.
Indologist Jan Wilhelm Boissevain earned his PhD at Leiden University by 1905, studying under doctoral supervisor Jacob Samuel Speyer.

Jan Willem de Jong was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Leiden, Harvard, and Paris under Bosch, Gonda, and others, later holding posts at Leiden University and Australian National University.

Jan de Vries was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and Indology who studied at the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University, where he also held a post from 1926 to 1946. He studied under Willibald Kirfel.

Jan van der Valk is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. He studied biology at KU Leuven (MSc 2005–2010) and anthropology at the University of Kent (PhD 2012–2016), later working as a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Vienna.

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch, a specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied under David P. Jackson and David Seyfort Ruegg. He held posts at Hamburg, Munich, Copenhagen (2003–2016), Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Ruhr University Bochum.
Janakiballav Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Surendranath Dasgupta. He held a post at Jadavpur University (attested 1977).
Janardan Mishra was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who served as Director of the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning (attested in 1959 and 1987).
Jane Bunnag was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of London by 1969 under the supervision of E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.
Jane Caple is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She held a post at the University of Leeds and is attested as a Research Fellow at the University of Manchester in 2026.

Jane Ellen Harrison was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Cheltenham Ladies' College, Newnham College, Cambridge, and under Robert Alexander Neil, later holding a post at Cambridge from circa 1898 to 1922.

Indologist and linguist Jane Helen Rowlands studied at Bangor University, Newnham College, Calcutta University (MA), and the Sorbonne/University of Paris (PhD). She later taught English at Karimganj College.

Jane-Marie Law is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who has held posts at Cornell University, including Director of Graduate Studies (attested 2008) and Associate Professor (attested 2026).

Janet Gyatso is a Tibetologist and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her BA, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley, and held posts at Stony Brook, Amherst College, and Harvard University, among others.

Janet R. Goodwin studied Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies at UC Berkeley under Delmer M. Brown and Britten Dean. She held posts attested in 1994 at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu.
Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Frances Wilson, and doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota.

Janice Dean Willis is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She earned degrees from Cornell and Columbia (PhD under Alex Wayman) and held posts at Wesleyan University (1977–2013) and Agnes Scott College.
